title: What's New in Kotlin Jump
tagline: The long dash leaves the window
summary: The long dash was banned from the README and the release notes and a script checked those. Nothing checked the extension itself, so it kept writing them in the window.

highlights.title: Reworded Where You Read It
highlights.description: 65 pieces of text: the What's New title, the Run Android App pickers, the pairing dialogs, the hovers, the suppression descriptions, the diagnostics, the chat answers, the logcat status bar.

highlights.title: A Bare Dash Meant Nothing
highlights.description: Two logcat status bar fields used a lone long dash to mean empty. They say none now, which a screen reader can read out.

sections.heading: Notes
bullets: The script that guards the README and the release notes now guards the sources too, and a check confirms it fails when a dash is put back in a window title.
The output channel keeps its own, on purpose: those lines are for whoever is debugging the extension, not copy anyone reads.
